title: IBM's Power11 Processor
problem: High-performance server and HPC workloads require next-generation processors with improved single-thread performance, power efficiency, and memory bandwidth.
motivation: Enterprise computing and scientific computing demand higher per-core performance and energy efficiency to handle complex workloads and machine learning tasks.
method: Power11 improves upon the POWER instruction set—the basic language processors understand—with faster internal circuits for executing instructions and a redesigned cache hierarchy (layered temporary fast memory that helps the processor access data more quickly). It enhances the memory controllers that manage data flow between the processor and main memory, and it includes specialized accelerator circuits designed to speed up specific workloads common in enterprise servers and supercomputing environments.
key_novelty: Power11 comprehensively improves the POWER processor architecture—with faster cores, better caching, improved memory bandwidth, and specialized accelerators—for high-performance enterprise and supercomputing workloads.
contributions: Enhanced memory system and cache hierarchy
